public_rationale: On 23 September 2026, Anthropic announced a Claude-led enzyme discovery with CRISPR-like repeats. That afternoon at the UN, Amodei said it 'may constitute a new gene editing mechanism' with possible gene-therapy uses. Le Grand Continent reports that Amodei himself compared the enzymes to CRISPR in his announcement. The preprint had not yet shown that the enzyme is active, and a CRISPR researcher said presenting early results as a major discovery was unhelpful. So the core claim holds: Amodei compared the discovery to CRISPR-style gene editing before its function had been shown. Two caveats: in the speech he called the finding 'preliminary' and did not name CRISPR, and one critic says he stated nothing false.
limitations: If the claim covers only the UN speech, the CRISPR comparison there is implicit and hedged as 'preliminary'.
'Overhyped' is a value judgment, so I tested only the checkable core.
The automated transcript is not the official record.

our_interpretation: Plain reading: on 23 September 2026, Amodei compared Anthropic's newly announced enzyme system to CRISPR or to CRISPR-style gene editing, before the system's function had been shown.
The footnote sits in a passage about the speeches, but the sentence does not limit the comparison to the speech. I count Amodei's speech and his announcement post that same day.
'Overhyped' is a judgment. I test the checkable core: that he made the comparison, and that function had not yet been shown.
criteria.support_condition: Amodei compared the discovery to CRISPR or CRISPR-style gene editing on 23 September 2026, while the preprint or experts say the system's function had not yet been shown.
criteria.contradiction_condition: Amodei made no such comparison that day, or the system's gene-editing function had already been shown when he spoke.
